metadata.source: Adapted from Forbidden Lands Core Rules and period American frontier material culture
metadata.region: American West (Great Plains, high desert, mountain territories)

items.name: Bowie Knife
items.notes: Heavy fighting/utility knife. Found on nearly every belt west of the Mississippi.

items.name: Skinning Knife
items.notes: Small curved blade for processing hides.

items.name: Hatchet
items.notes: Camp and utility axe, easily thrown.

items.name: Felling Axe
items.notes: Two-handed woodcutter's axe, devastating if pressed into combat.

items.name: Machete
items.notes: Long clearing blade, common among border-country ranch hands.

items.name: Tomahawk
items.notes: Light hand axe, can be thrown at Short range.

items.name: Knuckleduster
items.notes: Concealable brass knuckles.

items.name: Cavalry Saber
items.notes: Curved military blade, mostly seen on ex-soldiers and cavalry veterans.

items.name: Straight Razor
items.notes: Barber's blade, easily concealed.

items.name: Bull Whip
items.notes: Leather cattle whip. Little damage but excellent for controlling animals or intimidation.

items.name: Branding Iron
items.notes: Ranch tool, brutal when heated and swung.

items.name: Pickaxe
items.notes: Prospector's mining tool, unwieldy but heavy.

items.name: Sharpened Shovel
items.notes: Digging tool with a filed edge, common improvised weapon. See also Shovel (Digging) under Tools for the unmodified version.

items.name: Pitchfork
items.notes: Farm tool with two or three tines.

items.name: Blacksmith's Hammer
items.notes: Heavy forging hammer, devastating but unwieldy.

items.name: Sledgehammer
items.notes: Two-handed railroad spike hammer.

items.name: Club
items.notes: Simple wooden cudgel or pick handle.

items.name: Walking Cane
items.notes: Occasionally conceals a hidden blade in finer models.

items.name: Single-Action Revolver (.45 Colt)
items.notes: The standard sidearm of the era, also known as the Army Revolver. Six-shot cylinder, reliable and widespread, Long range.

items.name: Pocket Revolver (.32)
items.notes: Small, easily concealed backup gun.

items.name: Cap-and-Ball Revolver (Pre-War Surplus)
items.notes: Older percussion revolver, slow to reload but still deadly.

items.name: Navy Revolver (.36 cal)
items.notes: Cap-and-ball six-shooter, Short range only.

items.name: LeMat Revolver
items.notes: Nine-shot cylinder plus a single shotgun barrel usable as a Slow Action. Short/Long range.

items.name: Derringer
items.notes: Two-shot hideout gun favored by gamblers.

items.name: Lever-Action Rifle (Winchester-pattern)
items.notes: Fast-firing repeating rifle, the standard long gun of the era.

items.name: Single-Shot Trapdoor Rifle
items.notes: Military-surplus breechloader, slower but accurate at range.

items.name: Buffalo Rifle
items.notes: Heavy long-range hunting rifle (a Sharps-pattern .52 cal), devastating but slow to reload. Capped at G3 like all other firearms.

items.name: Double-Barrel Shotgun
items.notes: Brutal at close range, favored by stagecoach guards and saloon keepers.

items.name: Single-Barrel Shotgun
items.notes: Break-action, one shell, Short range. Scatters for +1 damage at Arm's Length.

items.name: Sawed-Off Shotgun
items.notes: Cut down for concealment, devastating at arm's reach but useless at range.

items.name: Carbine
items.notes: Shortened cavalry rifle, easy to handle on horseback.

items.name: Hunting Bow
items.notes: Traditional bow, still used by some native hunters and scouts. Silent.

items.name: War Bow
items.notes: Heavier bow built for hunting and defense.

items.name: Sling
items.notes: Improvised herder's tool, effective against varmints.

items.name: Throwing Knife
items.notes: Balanced blade for throwing.

items.name: Pistol Cartridges (box of 25, .45)
items.notes: Standard revolver ammunition.

items.name: Rifle Cartridges (box of 20)
items.notes: Standard rifle/carbine ammunition.

items.name: Shotgun Shells (box of 10)
items.notes: Buckshot and birdshot loads.

items.name: Arrows (bundle of 12)
items.notes: Wood shafts with steel or flint heads.

items.name: Percussion Caps (tin of 100)
items.notes: Required for cap-and-ball firearms.

items.name: Thick Clothing
items.notes: Layered work clothes. Minimal but genuine protection.

items.name: Leather Vest
items.notes: Thickened leather vest. Minimal but genuine protection against blades and glancing blows.

items.name: Thick Leather Duster
items.notes: Long oiled leather coat, thickened for protection. Turns weather and blunts a knife's edge, no defense against a bullet.

items.name: Sheepskin Coat
items.notes: Heavy winter coat. Some cushioning value, mostly protection from the cold.

items.name: Padded Work Coat
items.notes: Quilted cotton coat worn by laborers.

items.name: Buffalo Hide Coat
items.notes: Thick, heavy hide coat favored by trappers and buffalo hunters. Best protection short of true armor, and rare for it.

items.name: Cavalry Tunic (Surplus)
items.notes: Ex-military wool tunic with reinforced shoulders.

items.name: Chest Bandolier
items.notes: Cartridge belt worn across the chest; negligible protection but iconic.

items.name: Metal Breastplate
items.notes: Almost unheard of outside bizarre circumstances. -1 to AGILITY rolls while worn.

items.name: Wide-Brim Hat
items.notes: Standard frontier headwear. No real protection, essential against sun and rain.

items.name: Canvas Saddlebag
items.notes: Pair of bags slung over a saddle. Holds roughly 15 kg.

items.name: Leather Satchel
items.notes: Sturdy shoulder bag.

items.name: Canvas Rucksack
items.notes: Holds roughly 20 kg, worn on the back.

items.name: Wooden Trunk
items.notes: Locked chest for valuables, common in homesteads and rail depots.

items.name: Coin Pouch
items.notes: Small leather pouch for coin and dust.

items.name: Canteen
items.notes: Tin or leather-covered water flask, holds ~1 liter.

items.name: Gun Belt with Holster
items.notes: Belt and holster for a revolver, often with a cartridge loop.

items.name: Rifle Scabbard
items.notes: Saddle-mounted rifle sheath.

items.name: Bedroll
items.notes: Blanket roll for sleeping outdoors.

items.name: Dynamite (1 stick)
items.notes: Blast weapon, requires a fuse. Capped at G3 like all other Gear bonuses.

items.name: Medical Kit
items.notes: +1 Gear bonus to HEALING rolls, 3 uses before resupply. A lighter field kit; see Medical Bag for a full surgeon's set.

items.name: Mining Supplies
items.notes: +1 Gear bonus to SURVIVAL rolls when Prospecting; a pan, pick, and sieve bundled together. See also Prospector's Pan and Assay Kit.

items.name: Lantern
items.notes: Kerosene lantern with glass chimney.

items.name: Matches (box of 50)
items.notes: Friction matches, a modern convenience of the era.

items.name: Flint and Steel
items.notes: Older fire-starting method, backup when matches run out.

items.name: Rope (10m)
items.notes: Hemp rope for climbing, hauling, or tying off a horse.

items.name: Lasso
items.notes: Braided rawhide lariat for roping cattle.

items.name: Hobbles
items.notes: Leather straps to restrict a horse's movement while grazing.

items.name: Prospector's Pan
items.notes: Shallow metal pan for panning gravel and silt.

items.name: Assay Kit
items.notes: Small scale and acid kit for testing ore purity.

items.name: Farrier's Kit
items.notes: Tools for shoeing horses on the trail.

items.name: Medical Bag
items.notes: A sawbones' kit — bandages, laudanum, surgical tools.

items.name: Sewing Kit
items.notes: Needle, thread, and patches for mending.

items.name: Carpenter's Tools
items.notes: Saw, hammer, and chisel set.

items.name: Fishing Line and Hook
items.notes: Simple line and hook for river fishing.

items.name: Steel Traps (pair)
items.notes: Leg-hold traps for small game and fur.

items.name: Shovel (Digging)
items.notes: For prospecting, grave-digging, or trench work.

items.name: Whetstone
items.notes: For sharpening blades.

items.name: Gun Cleaning Kit
items.notes: Oil, rag, and rod for maintaining firearms.

items.name: Deck of Cards
items.notes: For poker, faro, or passing a long night.

items.name: Bible or Prayer Book
items.notes: Well-worn, often carried by preachers and the devout.

items.name: Pocket Watch
items.notes: Mechanical pocket watch, a mark of some means.

items.name: Telegraph Key (Portable)
items.notes: Field telegraph set for tapping into a line.

items.name: Branding Kit
items.notes: Iron brand and portable forge for marking cattle.

items.name: Hardtack (portion)
items.notes: Dense biscuit, keeps for months.

items.name: Salt Pork (portion)
items.notes: Cured pork, trail staple.

items.name: Beans (sack)
items.notes: Dried beans, cheap and filling.

items.name: Coffee (pouch)
items.notes: Ground or bean coffee, near-universal trail necessity.

items.name: Jerky (portion)
items.notes: Dried, smoked meat.

items.name: Cornmeal (sack)
items.notes: Ground corn, staple for johnnycake and mush.

items.name: Whiskey (bottle)
items.notes: Rough frontier whiskey, currency in its own right.

items.name: Sugar (pouch)
items.notes: Refined or raw sugar.

items.name: Canned Peaches
items.notes: A rare luxury, tinned fruit shipped in by rail.

items.name: Cattle Hide (bundle)
items.notes: Raw cowhide, valuable to tanneries.

items.name: Beaver Pelts (bundle)
items.notes: Prime fur, still valuable though the trade has declined.

items.name: Silver Ore (sack)
items.notes: Unrefined ore, worth assaying before sale.

items.name: Gold Dust (small pouch)
items.notes: Panned gold dust, common frontier currency in mining camps.

items.name: Wool (bale)
items.notes: Sheared wool, shipped east by rail.

items.name: Buffalo Hides (bundle)
items.notes: Increasingly scarce as the herds are hunted out.

items.name: Barbed Wire (roll)
items.notes: New invention fencing the open range, a point of bitter dispute among ranchers.

items.name: Iron Nails (keg)
items.notes: Essential for construction, shipped in by rail.

items.name: Tobacco (pouch)
items.notes: Chewing or smoking tobacco.

items.name: Riding Horse
items.notes: Standard saddle horse, essential for frontier travel.

items.name: Cow Pony
items.notes: Sturdy, hardy horse bred for ranch work.

items.name: Draft Mule
items.notes: Reliable pack and cart animal.

items.name: Cavalry Horse (Trained)
items.notes: Trained for gunfire and combat, very expensive.

items.name: Milk Cow
items.notes: Homestead dairy animal.

items.name: Ox Team (pair)
items.notes: Slow but strong draft team for wagons and plows.

items.name: Buckboard Wagon
items.notes: Light, versatile open wagon.

items.name: Chuck Wagon
items.notes: Mobile kitchen wagon for cattle drives.

items.name: Covered Wagon
items.notes: Canvas-topped wagon for long-distance hauling and family travel.

items.name: Mining Cart
items.notes: Rail-mounted ore cart for mine tunnels.

items.name: Rowboat
items.notes: Small river craft.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Outlaw
npc_equipment_sets.description: A wanted man living by the gun.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Lawman
npc_equipment_sets.description: A sheriff or deputy keeping the peace.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Rancher
npc_equipment_sets.description: A working cattle rancher or ranch hand.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Prospector
npc_equipment_sets.description: An independent silver or gold prospector.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Native Scout
npc_equipment_sets.description: A scout caught between two worlds, tracking and guiding.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Gambler
npc_equipment_sets.description: A card sharp working saloons and stage towns.

npc_equipment_sets.name: Drifter
npc_equipment_sets.description: A wanderer with little more than what he carries.
